articles.title: Alcaraz se pronuncia sobre la vuelta de Ferrero: "Entrene al jugador que entrene, creo que le irá muy bien"
articles.standfirst: El murciano habló en exclusiva con el periodista británico James Gray en el marco de la Laver Cup en Londres
articles.summary: El murciano habló en exclusiva con el periodista británico James Gray en el marco de la Laver Cup en Londres
articles.body: Desde que Juan Carlos Ferrero anunciara el pasado 16 de septiembre su regreso 'a los ruedos' como entrenador la próxima temporada sin revelar la identidad del jugador, el mundillo del tenis vive expectante por saber a quién va a dirigir el hombre que llevó a la cima a Carlos Alcaraz. Sin embargo, el murciano no había hablado hasta ahora del regreso de su ex técnico al circuito. Ha tenido que ser en el marco de la Laver Cup donde el ganador de siete grandes ha opinado por fin de la vuelta de 'Juanki'. Carlos ha ofrecido una entrevista en exclusiva al periodista británico James Gray, editor de deportes en The i Paper y copresentador del podcast Tennis Unfiltered. Gray ha querido saber de primera mano cómo se siente el tenista de El Palmar con la noticia y las palabras de éste no han podido ser más amables: "Estoy muy feliz de que vaya a volver al circuito y verle de nuevo por aquí. Va a ser genial. Entrene al jugador que entrene, creo que le irá muy bien". Alcaraz y Ferrero separaron sus caminos el 17 de diciembre de 2025. Fue el murciano el que lo hizo público con un mensaje en sus redes sociales. Atrás quedaban más de siete años de relación -desde agosto de 2018- en los que consiguieron juntos 24 títulos, incluidos seis de Grand Slam. El regreso de Ferrero es una auténtica bomba dentro del circuito, sobre todo si toma las riendas de una estrella que compita directamente con Alcaraz por el número 1 y los grandes títulos. De momento toca esperar pero Carlos no ha podido ser más cariñoso, demostrando que el agradecimiento por todo lo vivido está por encima de todo.

articles.title: Rafa Jódar, todo por Europa: rompe los cordones de su zapatilla en su victoria ante Bublik
articles.standfirst: El madrileño debuta con victoria en la Laver Cup y vuelve a poner por delante a Europa 2-1
articles.summary: El madrileño debuta con victoria en la Laver Cup y vuelve a poner por delante a Europa 2-1
articles.body: El equipo europeo de la Laver Cup tiene una mina de oro en la figura de Rafa Jódar. Lo que España ya había comprobado el pasado fin de semana en tierras chilenas, donde el joven madrileño tan sólo cedió dos juegos ante Cristian Garín en el segundo mejor debut de un miembro de la Armada, lo supo este viernes el resto del mundo. Jódar, en su estreno oficial en la competición organizada por Roger Federer, dio buena cuenta de Alexander Bublik, por 6-2 y 6-3. Para Rafa todo lo justifica el objetivo final de la victoria. Su intensidad en los apoyos provocó que en el segundo juego del primer set se cargara literalmente los cordones de una de sus zapatillas. Lo curioso fue cuando acudió a la silla de cambios para que el capitán Yannik Noah le ayudara. En los torneos del circuito esa función recae en su padre y entrenador. Tanto le costó a Noah que Flavio Cobolli y Alexander Zverev, compañeros de equipo de Jódar, se ofrecieron y prepararon otras zapatillas en caso de que el español tuviera un nuevo percance. El tenista de Leganés, el 14 de las listas ATP, es un competidor nato. Iba camino del rosco en la segunda manga, como ya hizo con Garín en la Davis. Bublik, el 21 del mundo, fue capaz de atajar a tiempo la sangría para maquillar el resultado. El punto de Rafa seguro no será el último que consigue defendiendo los intereses de Europa. Roger Federer y Tony Godsick le tienen en su agenda para próximas ediciones.

articles.title: Laver Cup: Carlos Alcaraz, Jakub Mensik win doubles to put Team Europe 3-1 up vs Team World after opening day in London
articles.summary: Opening day of 2026 Laver Cup in London sees Team Europe move into 3-1 lead vs Team World; Casper Ruud, Rafael Jodar bank singles wins; Carlos Alcaraz and Jakub Mensik win doubles; Watch the Laver Cup at The O2 in London from 25-27 September live on Sky Sports Tennis
articles.body:
Alcaraz and Mensik beat Alexander Bublik and Taylor Fritz 6-4 6-4 in the final match of the day at the O2 Arena in London.

Rafael Jodar had broken a 1-1 deadlock after the day session by defeating Bublik 6-2 6-3 in the evening's singles match.

In the day session, Brandon Nakashima made the most of his Laver Cup debut by beating Mensik 6-1 3-6 10-7.

In the event's opener, Casper Ruud beat Francisco Cerundolo 6-7 (4-7) 6-4 10-8 to give Europe an early lead. There are four matches per day in the three-day event.

The 16th-ranked Nakashima was a late addition to Andre Agassi's roster after US Open runner-up Ben Shelton withdrew last week.

Following the completion of the opening day, Alcaraz said: "I'm just trying to have fun in every place that I go and on every court that I play on.

"I don't usually play doubles. I just ​try to enjoy and be better at things. I use doubles to try and improve my ⁠tennis, a couple of adjustments. Having a partner like Jakub, ⁠it's really easy to have fun on the court."

Wins are worth one point on Friday, two points on Saturday and three points on Sunday. The first team to reach 13 points wins.

Europe have won the Laver Cup five times while Team World won their third title in last year's edition of the Ryder Cup-style event.

articles.title: Jódar y sus razones para romper los cordones: "Es por cómo me deslizo en pista dura y cuando corro a la red"
articles.standfirst: El madrileño reconoce que le encanta la competición por equipos
articles.summary: El madrileño reconoce que le encanta la competición por equipos
articles.body: Rafa Jódar ha vuelto a romper los cordones de sus zapatillas al principio de su partido de la Laver Cup con Alexander Bublik. A la conclusión, el madrileño ha dado su explicación de por qué se repite esa imagen en algunos torneos del calendario tenístico. "Es la manera como me deslizo en pista dura, cuando pego la derecha o cuando corro hacia la red. Por suerte tengo muchas zapatillas preparadas", reflexiona. Roger Federer no se ha perdido la exhibición del madrileño ante Alexander Bublik y ha seguido su partido desde la primera final de la grada del 02 Arena de Londres. "Que Federer haya visto mi partido significa mucho para mí y hacer una mención especial también a Rod Laver", reflexionaba el joven madrileño. Este tiene claro cuáles son sus objetivos: "Mi principal objetivo es mejorar. Siempre he trabajado muy duro para llegar donde estoy ahora pero quiero más. Y quiero ser mejor para competir con los mejores". Rafa confiesa que, desde el primer momento, se ha sentido respaldado por parte de Carlos Alcaraz: "Carlos me ha ayudado mucho desde que llegué a Londres y sabe más que yo como funciona este torneo porque ya había estado antes. Que hay dos españoles siempre ayuda , el idioma siempre ayuda".

articles.standfirst: El murciano suma ya 16 puntos defendiendo al equipo europeo en tres ediciones
articles.summary: El murciano suma ya 16 puntos defendiendo al equipo europeo en tres ediciones
articles.body: A Carlos Alcaraz le encantan competir por equipos y por ahí se entienden sus buenos resultados en la Laver Cup, evento que tiene a Mercedes-Benz de patrocinador global. En el 02 Arena de Londres, en su tercera participación en el certamen, Carlitos ya suma 16 puntos para Europa tras ganar este viernes a Alexander Bublik y Taylor Fritz, por 6-4 y 6-4. Se sitúa a dos puntos de Roger Federer, tercero en la clasificación histórica de puntuación, con 18. Por delante del suizo están Alexander Zverev, con 21, y Jack Sock, con 20. Alcaraz atrapará a Federer si gana este sábado su partido individual y tiene opciones matemáticas de terminar la Laver Cup como el mayor ganador de la historia en función de los resultados de su compañero Zverev.

articles.body: Lo que el viernes fue un duelo de dobles será este sábado un partido de individuales. Carlos Alcaraz y Taylor Fritz se vieron las caras en el cierre de la primera jornada de la Laver Cup haciendo pareja con Jakub Mensik y Alexander Bublik, respectivamente. El segundo día de competición se miden en individuales. Alcaraz domina los precedentes entre ambos por cinco victorias a una. Precisamente el único triunfo del estadounidense data de la Laver Cup 2025 en San Francisco. El precedente más reciente fueron las ATP Finals de Turín. El partido entre Carlos Alcaraz y Taylor Fritz, de la segunda jornada de la Laver Cup, se jugará a las 20.00 horas en España en la central del O2 Arena de Londres, en el inicio de la sesión nocturna del sábado. articles.title: Davidovich regresa con fuerza dos meses después y pasa a cuartos del torneo de Chengdu
articles.standfirst: El malagueño derrotó al argentino Juan Manuel Cerúndolo en dos sets y se las verá con el 'qualy' Muller
articles.summary: El malagueño derrotó al argentino Juan Manuel Cerúndolo en dos sets y se las verá con el 'qualy' Muller
articles.body: Alejandro Davidovich, el único español que ha iniciado ya la gira asiática, se ha clasificado este sábado para los cuartos del Open 250 de Chengdu tras derrotar al argentino Juan Manuel Cerúndolo, por un doble 6-4. El tenista de Fuengirola, de 27 años, ha regresado con fuerza a la competición tras verse obligado a parar por culpa de una lesión en la espalda. Davidovich se las verá en cuartos con el francés Alexandre Muller, el 135 del rabking ATP y procedente de la previa. Muller llegó a estar el 38 del mundo en agosto de 2025. En parte gracias a su título en Hong Kong. Álex es uno de los cinco jugadores españoles que opta a una de las dos plazas restantes para entrar en el equipo español de la Copa Davis que jugará la fase final de Bolonia (24 al 29 de noviembre). Carlos Alcaraz, Rafa Jódar y Marcel Granollers estarán seguro en el quinteto. El malagueño ya entraba en los planes del capitán David Ferrer para los 'playoff' de Chile si no hubiese tenido el percance físico que le ha dejado sin competir los dos últimos meses. Davidovich ya ha demostrado sobradamente sus aptitudes en superficie dura bajo techo, el hábitat en el que se jugará el título de la Ensaladera de plata. La pasada campaña, sin ir más lejos, terminó el curso con los cuartos de Bruselas, la final de Basilea y los octavos del Masters 1000 de París. El español es el segundo cabeza de serie del cuadro de Chengdu. El primero es el monegasco Valentin Vacherot.

articles.title: Rafa Jódar y su encuentro con Roger Federer: "Hablé con él y significa mucho para mí que me viera jugar"
articles.standfirst: El madrileño destaca su vocación adquirida por los equipos en su etapa universitaria
articles.summary: El madrileño destaca su vocación adquirida por los equipos en su etapa universitaria
articles.body: Rafa Jódar ha debutado, en el margen de ocho días, en el equipo de Copa Davis que selló en tierras chilenas el billete a las Finales de Bolonia y en la Laver Cup 2026 de Londres, con Mercedes-Benz de patrocinador global. En ambos casos saboreó la victoria con sendas palizas a Cristian Garín (6-0 y 6-2) y Alexander Bublik (6-2 y 6-3). Siete juegos cedidos en dos partidos con un denominador común: se trataba de competiciones por equipos. "La universidad me ayudó a acostumbrarme a este tipo de torneos por equipos. Estaba en Virginia, en un ambiente que me ayudó mucho. Crecí y maduré mucho como jugador. Ahora al competir por equipos me siento más preparado y todo el trabajo del año pasado me ayuda en cierto modo a afrontar este tipo de partidos", reflexiona en MARCA el joven valor de la Armada. Jódar coincidió por primera vez con Roger Federer durante la gala de la Laver Cup celebrada la noche del jueves en Londres. "Hablé con él y es una gran persona fuera de la pista. Que estuviera viendo mi partido con Bublik significa mucho para mí, es una leyenda del tenis y todo este torneo involucra todo el trabajo que Roger ha estado haciendo estos últimos años. La Laver Cup es muy importante para el tenis porque juegas por equipos y es algo a lo que no estamos muy acostumbrados. Es una semana donde puedes disfrutar mucho y aprender a la vez".

articles.title: 'All golds will go to India': Soft Tennis makes bold claim in 2030 CWG push
articles.summary: New Delhi: Jay Meena's big promise came within days of creating history at Aichi-Nagoya.
articles.body: New Delhi: Jay Meena's big promise came within days of creating history at Aichi-Nagoya. The Asian Games bronze medallist didn't hesitate before making a bold prediction: if soft tennis is included at the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad, “all the gold will remain in India.”It wasn't a throwaway celebration line. It has become the rallying cry of Indian soft tennis.Days after Meena became the country's first Asian Games medallist in the sport, officials are shifting their focus from Nagoya to Ahmedabad, where they believe India's biggest opportunity lies — not just to make numbers, but to make it into a medal bonanza at the Commonwealth Games.A historic bronze changes the conversationFor the Amateur Soft Tennis Federation of India (ASTFI), Meena's breakthrough is more than an individual achievement. It is validation of a project that began in 2002, when the sport was first introduced in India.“This is definitely a historical moment for India,” Harshang Khodadhara, Special Advisor to ASTFI and the International Soft Tennis Federation (ISTF), told TimesofIndia.com.ALSO READ | Jay Meena battled typhoid, hip injury and self-doubt to win historic Asian Games medal“We participated in four Asian Games and won a medal in the fourth. We don't want to stay in bronze. Our next target is silver or gold. We want to win a silver, at least, in singles competition. I am not being arrogant here. Japan and South Korea are at the next level. But definitely, with the support of the government, we will beat them,” he continued.The federation believes the medal finally gives the sport the visibility it has long lacked despite receiving government recognition and Sports Authority of India (SAI) support.Why Ahmedabad 2030 mattersThe federation's immediate ambition extends beyond medals.Soft tennis is pushing to become part of the 2030 Commonwealth Games, which India will host in Ahmedabad. While the sport enjoys widespread popularity across East Asia, Commonwealth participation remains limited. Countries such as India, Pakistan and Bangladesh already compete regularly, while federations also exist in England and Australia, providing the foundation for broader expansion.Meena believes growing participation across Commonwealth nations is the final piece of the puzzle.“If European countries adopt this game, the chances of entering the Commonwealth Games become very good,” he said. “And if it is included, whether it's me or another Indian athlete, all the gold will remain in India,” he said confidently.Khodadhara echoes that confidence.“India is the highest-ranked team among Commonwealth nations. If soft tennis is included in 2030, we are assuring that all the gold will be in India,” he said, while adding that both the Gujarat and Central governments have been supportive of the sport's growth.Infrastructure exists alreadyUnlike emerging racket sports battling for court space, soft tennis requires remarkably little new investment.The sport uses the same dimensions and playing surface as lawn tennis. Lakhs of existing tennis courts can host competitions without modification.“From an infrastructure point of view, there is no issue,” Khodadhara explained. “The courts used in tennis are also used in soft tennis.”Meena made a similar argument after his medal, insisting India already possesses “lakhs of courts” and simply needs to identify and support talent rather than build new facilities.The gap between India and Asia's giantsIndia's confidence does not ignore reality, though. Japan and South Korea remain the sport's traditional powerhouses, having developed professional leagues and coaching systems over nearly a century. India, by comparison, has been playing organised soft tennis for just over two decades.That difference, Khodadhara says, is less about talent and more about exposure.“The biggest gap is international exposure. The techniques and skills are there. To implement and develop it here, we need more foreign coaches, more foreign exposure. As much as possible,” he explained.He highlighted another structural challenge: many state sports policies prioritise Olympic disciplines, leaving sports such as soft tennis, which are included at the Asian Games, but not the Olympics, in a limbo."In most states, the schemes for international players are only focused on Olympic sports. Whether that means giving support to the players, or cash prizes to the schemes. You have to remember that the Asian Games are an Olympic of Asia. articles.title: Svitolina le quita la corona a Italia y clasifica a Ucrania para la final de la BJK Cup de Shenzhen
articles.standfirst: La ucraniana supera a Paolini en dos sets y hace buena la primera victoria de Kalinina ante Caterina Grant
articles.summary: La ucraniana supera a Paolini en dos sets y hace buena la primera victoria de Kalinina ante Caterina Grant
articles.body: Italia ha perdido una eliminatoria de la Billie Jean King Cup tres años después y le ha costado este sábado la eliminación en las semifinales de la edición de 2026 que se celebran en la ciudad china de Shenzhen. Ucrania ha ejercido de verdugo del equipo transalpino en el que su líder, Jasmine Paolini, perdió el segundo y definitivo punto ante Elina Svitolina, por 6-2 y 6-2. La número 1 ucraniana se quitó la espina de la derrota del jueves ante la belga Greet Minnen. Svitolina certificó el marcador de 2-0 tras el primer triunfo de su compatriota Anhelina Kalinina frente a Tyra Caterina Grant, por 6-3 y 6-4. La campeona de las dos últimas BJK Cup se ha quedado con las ganas de llegar al dobles donde siempre son favoritas con Paolini y su inseparable Sara Errani. Ucrania sigue adelante, a pesar de contar con la sensible baja de Marta Kostyuk, la décima raqueta de la WTA. En la final de este domingo espera la todopoderosa República Checa de Linda Noskova y Karolina Muchova. Los 11 títulos de las checas contrastan con la primera final de sus rivales.

articles.title: Tien derrota a Cobolli en el súper 'tie break' y pone más emoción a la Laver Cup
articles.standfirst: Europa y el Resto del Mundo igualan a tres puntos tras la disputa de cinco partidos
articles.summary: Europa y el Resto del Mundo igualan a tres puntos tras la disputa de cinco partidos
articles.body: A pesar de la teórica superioridad por nombres del equipo europeo de la Laver Cup, el Resto del Mundo sigue plantando cara este fin de semana en el O2 Arena de Londres. El viejo continente se marchó a dormir el viernes con una renta de 3-1, que ha sido liquidada por Learner Tien en el primer partido de la segunda jornada. Su triunfo ante Flavio Cobolli, por 6-3, 2-6 y 10-7, en el súper 'tie break', firma las tablas en la novena edición del torneo ideado por Roger Federer y que tiene a Mercedes-Benz de patrocinador global. Tien fue el último en ingresar en las convocatorias como sustituto del lesionado Ben Shelton. Ha respondido a la confianza del capitán Andre Agassi en su primera participación. A continuación, saltará a la pista del O2 Arena Alexander Zverev, número dos mundial y flamante campeón de Roland Garros y el US Open. Yannick Noah pone todo lo que tiene. En la sesión nocturna también aparecerá Carlos Alcaraz.

articles.title: De Miñaur frena la racha de Zverev con una gran remontada
articles.standfirst: El australiano, que levantó una bola de partido en el súper 'tie break', sitúa un 3-5 para el Resto del Mundo en la Laver Cup
articles.summary: El australiano, que levantó una bola de partido en el súper 'tie break', sitúa un 3-5 para el Resto del Mundo en la Laver Cup
articles.body: Alexander Zverev, el tenista más en forma del momento, ha encajado una dolorosa derrota este sábado en la segunda jornada de la Laver Cup 2026. Zverev demostró su buen momento en la consecución de su segundo Grand Slam en el US Open, seis días después en la serie de Copa Davis ante Croacia en Halle, pero no ha tenido continuidad en el 02 de Londres. Alex de Miñaur ha ejercido de verdugo, por 2-6, 7-6(5) y 11-9, para dar la primera ventaja al Resto del Mundo, 3-5. Nadie ha ganado más puntos que Zverev en la historia de la competición, con 21. Uno más de Jack Sock, y tres más que Roger Federer, que cierra el podio de ese ranking. De Miñaur acabó con una racha de nueve victorias consecutivas de su rival, además de levantar un 5-3 en la segunda manga y una pelota de partido en el súper 'tie break'. Álex creyó hasta el final, apoyado por su capitán Andre Agassi y el resto del equipo.

articles.title: Naomi Osaka heard a 9-year-old’s tennis dream in Cameroon, then made an unexpected move that could change the young player’s journey and take her closer to the biggest stage
articles.summary: Naomi Osaka's Play Academy grants 9-year-old Uma Bogso from Cameroon a scholarship to train at Mouratoglou Academy in France, transforming her tennis dreams into reality.
articles.body: Naomi Osaka has had a big impact on tennis beyond her own Grand Slam career, with her Play Academy initiative to help girls access the sport. One story that stood out was that of Uma Bogso, a 9-year-old tennis player from Cameroon whose ambitions caught Osaka’s attention.The initiative did not let geography and limited resources define Uma’s opportunities, and it granted her a scholarship to train at the Mouratoglou Academy in France. The move was an opportunity for the young player to be exposed to professional coaching, high-level facilities and an international tennis environment that had previously been well beyond her regular training setup.Naomi Osaka backs Cameroonian tennis prodigy Uma Bogso with landmark scholarship to train at Mouratoglou Tennis AcademyIt started with Uma idolising Naomi Osaka and dreaming of being a professional tennis player. The Cameroonian player was only 9 years old and already playing the sport with far fewer resources than many young athletes training in established tennis systems.Play Academy with Naomi Osaka provided an individual scholarship that enabled Uma to attend the Mouratoglou Academy in France. The scholarship allowed the young player to train at a state-of-the-art tennis center, work with professional coaching staff and mingle with other junior players, Play Academy said.The scholarship was important, in part, because Play Academy was established primarily to help grassroots organisations, not to regularly fund individual athletes. Therefore, Uma’s case offered a unique opportunity in the initiative and illustrated how the situation of a particular young player could be given direct attention.The opportunity also created an environment for Uma that was built around athlete development. The Mouratoglou Academy says its methodology relies on individualised coaching, listening, performance development and helping athletes progress on and off the court.Scholarship detailInformationYoung playerUma BogsoAge at scholarship9 years oldCountryCameroonSportTennisSupport initiativePlay Academy with Naomi OsakaTraining destinationMouratoglou AcademyLocationBiot, near Nice, FranceMain opportunityProfessional coaching and advanced tennis facilitiesA childhood dream suddenly receives global attentionUma’s story demonstrates what a difference access can make at the very beginning of a young athlete’s development. Talent alone does not guarantee a pathway into competitive sport, especially where coaching, facilities, tournament exposure and financial resources are limited.Also, a new tennis environment can offer a 9-year-old player experiences that go beyond the improvement of individual strokes. Playing with different players can expose you to new standards of competition, new routines, and it can also show you what a longer-term pathway in tennis can look like.That wider development is in line with the philosophy of Play Academy. The initiative was launched in 2020 by Naomi Osaka, Nike and Laureus Sport for Good, with a stated aim of increasing girls’ participation in sport and supporting organisations working with girls in underserved communities.Naomi Osaka gives Uma Bogso landmark scholarshipNaomi Osaka’s involvement gave Uma’s story a key connection to a player who’s felt the pressure of top-tier tennis firsthand. Osaka has four Grand Slam singles titles and has used her platform to talk about the importance of creating opportunities for girls in sport. Osaka wanted other girls to have the same opportunities and role models on their own sporting journey that she had, Play Academy said.For Uma, the scholarship was a concrete training opportunity rooted in that larger mission. Instead of just receiving encouragement, she was able to move into a professional academy environment and work with coaches who were geared to develop junior players.The Mouratoglou Academy is located in Sophia Antipolis on the French Riviera, near Nice and Cannes. Today its facilities include 33 clay and hard courts, eight indoor courts, a fitness room, sports medicine facilities, swimming pools and accommodation options for young players.The academy also says its coaching philosophy is designed to fit individual athletes, rather than to use one method. Its methodology is based on listening to players, individual coaching, development of performance and continuous assessment.So the significance of the move is not just the number of hours spent on a tennis court. A structured academy can expose a young athlete to training habits, competition preparation and routines that are hard to replicate without access to specialised facilities.Naomi Osaka’s Play Academy expands global missionSupport for Uma is part of a much larger mission established through Play Academy with Naomi Osaka. Launched in Japan in 2020 with Nike and Laureus Sport for Good, the program has focused on supporting grassroots organisations using sport to create opportunities for girls.The initiative was based on a problem beyond the game of tennis. Financial, social and access barriers can make it more difficult for girls to continue to participate in sport. Play Academy has therefore adopted an approach that has included funding, capacity-building support and gender inclusive coaching and not just elite competition.Uma’s scholarship illustrated how that philosophy could intersect with an individual athlete whose circumstances were especially compelling. Going from Cameroon to a top European tennis academy was a chance to go from very little local resources to a very structured international training setting.For a player who was only 9 years old when the opportunity presented itself, the real value of it may not be in the immediate results, but in the doors it opened along the way. articles.title: Alcaraz salva dos bolas de partido a Fritz e iguala el récord de puntos ganados por Federer en la Laver Cup
articles.standfirst: El murciano suma 18 puntos en 10 partidos jugados, dos menos que la leyenda suiza
articles.summary: El murciano suma 18 puntos en 10 partidos jugados, dos menos que la leyenda suiza
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz, con apenas 23 años, es uno de los tenistas récord de la actualidad. El número 1 más joven de la historia, a la vez que el más precoz en ganar los cuatro títulos del Grand Slam, ya es el tercero en el ranking de puntos sumados en la Laver Cup. Los 18 que atesora, tras su victoria ante Taylor Fritz, por 6-3, 4-6 y 12-10, le igualan a Roger Federer. El suizo, presente en la grada del 02 como propietario de la competición, llegó a esa cifra tras la disputa de 12 partidos. Su bagaje es de ocho triunfos y cuatro derrotas, todas ellas en el dobles. Dos partidos menos ha necesitado Alcaraz, que ha decantado a su favor ocho de sus 10 duelos en el torneo por equipos que cumple su novena edición con Mercedes-Benz de patrocinador global. Por delante restan Alexander Zverev, con 21 puntos ganados, y Jack Sock, que tiene 20. Alcaraz es sinónimo de espectáculo y lo sabían los asistentes al 02 que llenaron las gradas. Carlitos se llevó todos los puntos espectaculares. Una dejada por aquí, un globo por allá, otra volea muerta, para deleite de los miembros del equipo europeo y sus dos capitanes, Yannick Noah y Tim Henman. Después de perder dos veces el saque en la manga inicial, el estadounidense reaccionó con una rotura en el tercer juego de la continuación. Esa pequeña renta le valió para firmas las tablas y llevar el desenlace al súper 'tie break'. Ganó el mejor y el mejor es Alcaraz. Lo hizo después de salvar dos bolas de partido, con 9-10 y 10-11. Y acabó su obra con otra dejada marca de la casa. Europa, 5; Resto del Mundo, 5.

articles.title: Sir Andy Murray: Former Wimbledon champion 'still plans to help' Jack Draper ahead of scheduled 2027 return
articles.summary: Former Wimbledon champion Sir Andy Murray has hinted that he 'still plans to help' Jack Draper after the former world No 4 returns from injury; watch the final day of the Laver Cup at The O2 in London live on Sky Sports Tennis on Sunday
articles.body:
Draper revealed that he would not be returning to tennis until 2027 at the earliest in an Instagram video released earlier in September, having missed all four Grand Slams in 2026 after continuing to struggle with a bone bruise in his dominant left arm.

Murray - who joined Draper's stream for a brief spell in the summer after he split with former coach Jamie Delgado - reasserted his desire to join back up with the Englishman once he returns to full fitness:

"Yeah, there's still plans to help him [Draper]," Murray told Sky Sports.

"I don't know where that is. I'm not entirely sure because his ranking will have dropped.

"I don't know if he would get into Australia and potentially relying on wild cards and things like that, so we'll see.

"Hopefully he'll be back on the court training again soon and getting ready for the new season - it has been an interesting year."

Draper said he was in a "difficult place" after his first-round defeat by Martin Landaluce in the Cincinnati Open in August, admitting he was struggling to escape the mental fatigue that had built up during 15 months of battling serious injury.

Murray acknowledged the challenges faced in his time coaching Draper, but asserted that he was still able to enjoy his limited time alongside the former world No 4.

"I've been doing a little bit of coaching, which I've enjoyed, but also Jack's had a few injuries and has been off the tour for quite a while, so I haven't been able to get into that quite as much as I would have liked.

"I do still enjoy coming and watching [tennis] a little bit, but I'm happy doing what I'm doing with my kids just now."

articles.title: Laver Cup: Carlos Alcaraz beats Taylor Fritz in thrilling final set tiebreak as Team Europe edge in front of Team World
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz beat Taylor Fritz after a thrilling final set tiebreak as Team Europe hold a narrow 7-5 lead over Team World heading into the Laver Cup final day; watch the final day of the Laver Cup at The O2 in London live on Sky Sports from 1pm on Sunday
articles.body:
Fritz's only career victory over Alcaraz came during Team World's win over Europe in last year's Laver Cup, but Alcaraz saved two match points against the American and came out on top in a Saturday that featured six match-deciding tiebreaks in eight matches.

The Spaniard served an ace on Fritz's first match point and then used a drop shot to save another, and Alcaraz finally won it on his third match point when Fritz got to his drop shot but couldn't get it back.

"The drop shot is part of my game," Alcaraz said. "So in those moments, in those really close and important moments, I tried to use it because it was a really good weapon for me in this match and obviously I've been practising the drops since I was a little kid."

Fritz played a clean match with only nine unforced errors to Alcaraz's 30. But Alcaraz led 42-20 in winners - often bringing the O2 Arena crowd to its feet, as Roger Federer and Andy Murray applauded from the front row.

It was Alcaraz's first singles match since he lost to Ben Shelton in a U.S. Open quarterfinal that ended at 3:33 a.m. He won a doubles match with Jakub Mensik on Friday.

Earlier, it was all Team World - which is captained by Andre Agassi - as Alex de Minaur had a 2-6, 7-6 (5), 11-9 comeback victory over Alexander Zverev and Learner Tien outlasted Flavio Cobolli 6-3, 2-6, 10-7.

In the final match of the day, Zverev partnered with Casper Ruud to beat Alexander Bublik and Brandon Nakashima 6-4 6-6 (9-7) in the crucial doubles match that secured Team Europe the overnight lead.

Wins are worth three points on Sunday. The first team to reach 13 points wins.

Europe has won the Laver Cup five times while Team World took its third title in last year's edition of the Ryder Cup-style event.

articles.title: Laver Cup: Carlos Alcaraz saves match points as Team Europe take lead
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz narrowly avoids back-to-back singles defeats for the first time in 18 months as Team Europe lead Team World at the Laver Cup.
articles.body:
Two-time Wimbledon champion Carlos Alcaraz narrowly avoided back-to-back singles defeats for the first time in 18 months as Team Europe took a 7-5 lead over Team World at the Laver Cup.

The world number three saved two match points before overcoming Taylor Fritz 6-3 4-6 13-11 in a dramatic deciding tie-break at London's O2 Arena.

It was Alcaraz's first singles outing since his late-night quarter-final exit to Ben Shelton at the US Open.

"The drop shot is part of my game," Alcaraz said after sealing victory with a trademark touch.

"In those really close and important moments, I tried to use it because it was a really good weapon for me in this match."

American Fritz, whose only previous victory against the Spaniard came during Team World's triumph in last year's competition, kept errors to a minimum.

However, Alcaraz struck 42 winners to Fritz's 20, bringing an audience that included Roger Federer and Andy Murray to their feet.

Facing match point at 8-9 down in the tie break, Alcaraz fired an ace before leaning on a drop shot to stave off a second. He converted his third match point when Fritz failed to retrieve another delicate drop shot over the net.

Earlier on Saturday, Andre Agassi's Team World had threatened to run away with things.

Alex de Minaur fought back from a set down to shock Alexander Zverev 2-6 7-6 (7-5) 11-9, while American debutant Learner Tien edged Italy's Flavio Cobolli 6-3 2-6 10-7.

Following Alcaraz's singles heroics, Zverev returned to the court alongside Casper Ruud to secure an important 6-4 7-6 (9-7) doubles victory over Alexander Bublik and Brandon Nakashima, keeping Europe ahead going into the final day.

Match wins are worth three points on Sunday, with the first team to reach 13 points lifting the trophy.

Europe are chasing their sixth Laver Cup title, while holders Team World are aiming for their third.

articles.body: Alejandro Davidovich ha regresado totalmente recuperado de sus problemas en la espalda. Así lo demuestran los resultados. A pesar del parón forzado de 72 días, que le obligó a borrarse de Estoril, los Masters 1000 de Montreal y Cincinnati, y el US Open, además de no poder jugar por España la serie de Copa Davis ante Chile, el malagueño se ha clasificado este domingo para las semifinales del Open 250 de Chengdu (China), en el inicio de la gira asiática. Davidovich, el 29 del ranking ATP a sus 27 años y segundo cabeza de serie en Chengdu, sube un escalón en la clasificación mundial en detrimento del carioca Joao Fonseca. El tenista de Fuengirola ha dado buena cuenta del francés Alexandre Muller, con un tanteo de 6-1 y 7-5. Muller, procedente de la previa, nunca pudo hacer frente al juego del pupilo de los hermanos Pato y Pepo Clavet. En las semifinales del lunes espera Nikoloz Basilashvili. El georgiano será el segundo rival consecutivo procedente de la 'qualy'. Basilashvili decantó a su favor el único precedente entre ambos, en los octavos de Metz 2021. Nikoloz es el quinto jugador de ranking más bajo en unas semifinales ATP en 2026. Es la tercera semifinal del curso pata Álex (la decimocuarta de su carrera), que ya estuvo entre los cuatro mejores en Adelaida y Mallorca. Este último torneo significó su primer título como profesional.

articles.title: Billie Jean King Cup: Czech Republic thrash Ukraine to win 12th title
articles.summary: The Czech Republic ease past Ukraine to win the Billie Jean King Cup for the 12th time thanks to wins for 2026 Wimbledon finalists Karolina Muchova and Linda Noskova.
articles.body:
Czech Republic eased past Ukraine to win the Billie Jean King Cup for the 12th time.

This year's Wimbledon finalists Linda Noskova and Karolina Muchova breezed past their opponents to secure a 2-0 victory and deny the Ukrainians a first title in the competition.

Muchova, the runner-up at Wimbledon, comfortably beat Anhelina Kalinina 6-2 6-3 in the opening singles match before Noskova's 6-3 ⁠7-6 (7-5) win over world number seven Elina Svitolina ‌secured the title.

It is the Czechs' first win at the event since 2018, making them the second-most successful nation in its history after the United States, who have 18 titles.

It was also a first win as captain for Barbora Strycova, who has three previous triumphs to her name as a player. As a team, they dropped just one set throughout the tournament.

The Czechs also knocked out Great Britain in the quarter-finals in Shenzhen, China, which led GB captain Anne Keothavong to describe them as "the strongest team here".

articles.title: La Europa de Alcaraz recupera el cetro de la Laver Cup con tres puntos más de Zverev
articles.standfirst: El alemán, verdugo de Tien, el que más puntuación presenta en la historia del torneo
articles.summary: El alemán, verdugo de Tien, el que más puntuación presenta en la historia del torneo
articles.body: La Laver Cup 2026 ya es historia, con el triunfo este domingo de Europa sobre el Resto del Mundo, por 13 a 5. El conjunto del Viejo Continente impuso la lógica para recuperar el cetro que habían perdido hace un año en San Francisco. La victoria fue tan contundente que Carlos Alcaraz y Rafa Jódar se quedaron sin disputar sus partidos individuales contra Álex de Miñaur y Taylor Fritz. El equipo anfitrión se anotó los últimos 10 puntos de la competición. El triunfo el sábado de De Miñaur sobre Zverev dejó un marcador parcial de 3-5. Los hombres de Andre Agassi no ganaron más. Jakub Mensik y Flavio Cobolli aceleraron el desenlace abriendo la jornada dominical con una remontada frente a Fritz y De Miñaur. Estos sucumbieron por 7-5 y 6-3. Sascha no falló después y tiró de jerarquía ante Learner Tien, por 7-6(3) y 6-3. Los aficionados, que prácticamente llenaban las gradas del 02 londinense, se quedaron con las ganas de ver un día más en directo la magia de Carlitos. El murciano, animando en todo momento a Zverev desde la banda, es un jugador de equipo y promete volver a la Laver Cup. Tien, una de las grandes promesas del tenis americano y vencedor de las Next Gen Finals 2025 en Jeddah —en el mismo hábitat de Londres— no le puso las cosas fáciles a su rival alemán, con dos grandes en sus vitrinas en el presente curso. Learner forzó la muerte súbita en la manga inicial e incluso tuvo una bola de set, con 5-6 al resto. Lanzó una derecha al pasillo del dobles. El americano perdió el 'tie break' y por ahí se le fueron las opciones de victoria. Los vencedores se reparten un millón y medio de dólares, a partes iguales. Eso significa 250.000 dólares para cada uno. Los perdedores se quedan sin premio oficial aunque cuentan con el fijo negociado de manera individual por participar. La próxima edición, la décima, se disputará del 24 al 26 de septiembre de 2027, en el Intuit Dome de Inglewood, en Los Ángeles. El palmarés, tras nueve ediciones, refleja seis trofeos a tres para los europeos, que ganan por calidad y cantidad. “Yo voy con ellos”, afirma Roger Federer, propietario y el que ideó el torneo junto a su representante Tony Godsick. En el otro lado de la balanza está Rod Laver, la leyenda que da nombre al evento y que apoya al combinado del resto del mundo.

articles.title: Laver Cup: US Open champion Alexander Zverev seals victory for Team Europe against Team World at London's O2
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz had to be content with a cheerleader role as Team Europe reclaim the Laver Cup with victory over Team World at the O2 in London with Alexander Zverev securing the winning points; you can watch the WTA 1000 China Open live on Sky Sports from Wednesday
articles.body:
Zverev, who won the French Open and US Open titles this year, lived up to his 'best player in the world' tag to secure Laver Cup success give rival Carlos Alcaraz the day off.

The German clinched the trophy for Team Europe after defeating Tien in the second match of Sunday's finale 7-6 (7-3) 6-3.

"I haven't won a match here in two years, so I'm happy that I did it today," said Zverev, who recorded his first Laver Cup singles victory since 2024.

"Massive credit to the entire Team World. They pushed us all the way again. They were champions last year. This year, we had a great team chemistry and I'm very happy that we won."

Zverev had been talked up by Alcaraz after recent Grand Slam wins before this Ryder Cup-style event at The O2, but he lost in the doubles on Friday and let slip multiple match points against Alex De Minaur on Saturday.

Alcaraz wrestled back the initiative at the end of day two before Zverev teamed up with Casper Ruud to triumph in the doubles and leave Team Europe only two victories from glory ahead of Sunday's session.

After initially falling a break behind, Cobolli and Mensik settled into their rhythm and took control, racing past Team World's De Minaur and Taylor Fritz 7-5 6-3 to stretch Europe's lead to 10-5.

Flavio Cobolli and Jakub Mensik moved the boys in blue a step closer by beating Fritz and De Minaur in the doubles, which opened the door for Zverev to bring a run of three defeats in four editions for Team Europe to an end.

Zverev struggled against rookie Tien, although did have the insurance policy of team-mate Alcaraz up next if required, but the two-time major winner secured victory to help Team Europe prevail in front of tournament co-founder Roger Federer, who was sitting alongside Hollywood A-lister Leonardo DiCaprio.

Seven-time Grand Slam champion Alcaraz, who returned at the US Open after a lengthy lay-off due to a wrist injury, had been scheduled to face Australian De Minaur in a later singles match.

Rising 20-year-old Spaniard Rafael Jodar was due to play Fritz, but ⁠neither match was needed after Zverev wrapped up the contest.

"We had three chances to close ​it out in the singles," Zverev added. "Especially with Carlos playing after me, I think ​that gives me a lot of confidence and gives me a little bit of freedom to play.

"But still, ​it was an incredibly tough match. Credit to Learner as well.

"I think Carlos is also very happy that ⁠I closed it out. And me too, by the way! I'm very happy that I won."

Europe have now won six of the nine editions.

Czechs claim 12th Billie Jean King Cup crown

Czech Republic brushed ‌aside Ukraine to win their 12th Billie Jean King Cup title in Shenzhen with Karolina ​Muchova and Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova delivering an unassailable 2-0 lead in the final.

Wimbledon runner-up Muchova swept past Anhelina Kalinina 6-2 6-3 in the opening singles ​rubber before Noskova toppled world No 7 Elina Svitolina 6-3 7-6 (7-5) to ‌seal the title.

The Czechs are the second-most successful nation in the history of the premier international women's team competition, behind the ​USA, who hold a record 18 titles.

Ukraine were seeking their first Billie Jean King Cup crown.

articles.body: Poco tiempo de celebración por la consecución de su segunda Laver Cup va a tener Carlos Alcaraz. El murciano se desplaza este lunes por la mañana a Tokio, su primera parada de una gira asiática que tendrá después continuación en el Masters 1000 de Shanghái. Alcaraz empezará el martes, el mismo día que aterriza en la capital japonesa, sus entrenamientos, según ha podido saber MARCA. Y es que el certamen de categoría 500 se inicia el miércoles 30 de septiembre y Carlitos es el defensor de la corona. La baja por fatiga de Ben Shelton le permite coger un poco de aire en sus aspiraciones de mantener el número tres mundial a finales de curso. La diferencia en el ranking ATP con el estadounidense es de tan sólo 380 puntos. El campeón de siete grandes no será el único español en el cuadro del Open 500 de Tokio. Junto a él estarán Rafa Jódar y Alejandro Davidovich. El madrileño, que también viaja desde Londres, donde ha acompañado a Carlitos en la consecución de la Laver Cup, será el cuarto cabeza de serie del cuadro. Jódar está a 491 puntos del 'top10' que cierra Álex de Miñaur.

articles.summary: El campeón de siete grandes habla de lo especial que es coincidir con Federer durante la Laver Cup
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz celebraba su segundo título de la Laver Cup en tres participaciones. El tenista, que ha regresado a lo grande tras su lesión en la muñeca derecha, habla de lo que le espera en el futuro inmediato: "Necesito partidos, ritmo y ver cómo va a reaccionar mi cuerpo. La Copa Davis es un gran objetivo porque tenemos un gran equipo y tenemos opciones de ganar" Sobre las condiciones físicas a las que llega a final de curso, tras el parón de cuatro meses y medio por la lesión, el murciano asegura que "he estado mucho tiempo parado y en la vuelta a la competición he tenido partido exigentes. Hoy me sentía cansado después de los días intensos del viernes y el sábado. Mentalmente sí que me siento fresco y tengo muchas ganas de lo que viene. Obviamente, siempre hemos visto que esta parte de temporada me costaba por el desgaste mental y físico, pero creo que este año vamos a intentar dar la talla en todos los torneos y son objetivos muy importantes para mí". Alcaraz jugará las ATP Finals de Turín antes de la fase final de la Copa Davis de Bolonia: "Los torneos bajo techo siempre vienen bien. Ganar en Turín, con los mejores jugadores, me daría una confianza grandísima de cara a la Davis. Este año tenemos un equipazo. Con Jódar, con Marcel en el dobles, con Pedrito, con Mérida, con Munar... Es una pena que no podamos ir 10 jugadores porque todos nos lo merecemos. Tenemos una muy buena oportunidad y vamos a intentar aprovecharla". Carlitos reconoce la importancia del título de la Laver Cup a estas alturas: "Ganar siempre es positivo. La verdad es que ver a los jugadores, desde fuera, su nivel, verme a mí en situaciones de estrés y ver cómo las he manejado, da mucha motivación. Vamos a intentar seguir de la mejor manera. Ahora vienen torneos importantes como son Tokio y Shanghái, que son muy chulos y tengo ganas de ir para allá y ver a los fans asiáticos".

articles.title: Laver Cup: Alexander Zverev beats Learner Tien to seal victory for Team Europe
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev recovers from his day two defeat by Alex de Minaur to beat Learner Tien and clinch the Laver Cup title for Team Europe on the final day.
articles.body:
Alexander Zverev beat Learner Tien on the final day of the Laver Cup to lead Team Europe to their sixth title.

US Open champion Zverev recovered from a disappointing defeat by Team World's Alex de Minaur on day two and eased to a 7-6 (7-3) 6-3 win over Tien at London's O2 Arena.

After Carlos Alcaraz's heroics kept Europe in contention after that loss on day two, Flavio Cobolli and Jakub Mensik beat De Minaur and Taylor Fritz in the doubles to extend their lead before Zverev's triumph.

Both wins took Europe's tally to the required 13 needed to win, which meant that Alcaraz was not required to play again.

"I haven't won a Laver Cup match in two years, so I'm happy I did it today," said Zverev.

"Massive credit to the entire Team World. They pushed us all the way again, they were champions last year. We have a great team chemistry, it was a team effort.

"Winning as a team, there's no better feeling in sports. We don't have enough of it in tennis."

The USA's Tien, 20, was making his Team World debut and held his nerve in the first set to force a tiebreak, but world number two Zverev took control in the second and closed out the victory in one hour and 49 minutes.

Zverev has been part of all six of Team Europe's Laver Cup wins, and has the most singles wins at the event with eight.

articles.body: Rafa Jódar ha hecho pleno. En su primera participación en la Laver Cup se lleva el trofeo a casa. El madrileño, a sus 20 años, se encuentra con opciones matemáticas de ser 'top10' en la próxima gira asiática, que para él son los torneos de Tokio y Shanghái. "El 'top10' no debe ser un objetivo, lo principal es acabar bien el año en los dos meses que quedan. Si no se consigue esa meta, intentar hacerlo lo mejor posible. La Copa Davis es una motivación extra. Va a ser el último torneo de este año y será especial si David, el capitán, cuenta confía en mí y me llama para ir a Bolonia. Yo estaré disponible", reflexiona. Rafa es consciente del potencial del equipo español, con una mezcla de juventud y veteranía: "Si Carlos también viene, tenemos un gran equipo. Es un objetivo que, si nos lo proponemos, lo podemos conseguir".

articles.body:
The IHSAA boys sectional pairings were revealed Sunday, Sept. 27.

The Southwestern Indiana area will compete in sectionals 5 through 12. The latest Indiana High School Tennis Coaches Association rankings feature three of those teams: Jasper at 9, Barr-Reeve at 14 and Gibson Southern at 28.

All eight sectional brackets are provided below with analysis.

NOTE: These will be updates with dates, times and results throughout the week, so keep this page bookmarked!

Match 3 : Match 1 winner vs Match 2 winner

No. 9 Jasper is the resounding favorite in Sectional 5. The Wildcats navigated this sectional with ease last season, winning 5-0 in the semifinal and championship rounds. Forest Park defeated Southridge (4-1) and Northeast Dubois (3-2) this season.

Match 3: Match 1 winner vs Match 2 winner

Sullivan (12-4) can be seen as the favorites in this sectional. At 13-6, North Daviess has enough talent too, but the Cougars lost to Sullivan 1-4 on September 15. The winner of the Match 2 seems likely to end up at regionals.

Match 1: Vincennes Rivet vs Vincennes Lincoln

South Knox earned a 3-2 win over Vincennes Lincoln on September 10 that finished close in No.1 singles and in both doubles matches. The two programs should find their way to the championship match.

No. 14 Barr-Reeve has lost just two matches to this point — No. 7 Bloomington South (2-3) and No. 9 Jasper (0-5). Loogootee, the only other team with a winning record in this sectional, lost 0-5 to the Vikings on September 2.

Match 2: Gibson Southern vs Wood Memorial

No. 28 Gibson Southern and Tecumseh have both won 18 matches this season. The Titans defeated the Braves 3-2 on September 17 in a match that came down to No. 2 singles. The two programs are certainly the favorites in this sectional, which should lead to a competitive championship match in Sectional 9.

Match 4: Match 2 winner vs Match 3 winner

Match 5: Match 3 winner vs. Match 4 winner

Central appears to be the favorite in this sectional. While the Bears lost 5-0 in the championship round to North Posey last season, they began this season winning 5-0 themselves against the Vikings.

Match 3: Evansville Christian vs Match 1 winner

Memorial looks to be the most likely winner of this sectional. The Tigers won two matches 3-2 against North this season. The Huskies should be their main competitor and won this sectional a year ago. Evansville Christian (11-4) is another team to watch for.

Castle looks to be the favorite in this sectional. The Knights have been ranked for a large part of this season. If there is a team to contend with them, it is Heritage Hills. The two programs met early in the season on August 18, a 5-0 win for Castle.

articles.summary: El serbio regresa a la competición tras caer fuera del 'top10' por culpa de su derrota a la primera en el US Open
articles.body: Novak Djokovic es el hombre récord del tenis y por eso está considerado el mejor jugador de la historia. Todas las grandes marcas le corresponden y una de ellas hace referencia a sus cifras en el China Open, torneo de categoría 500 que se celebra en Pekín. El serbio, de 39 años, debutará contra el portugués Nuno Borges como sexto cabeza de serie del cuadro y pondrá en juego su condición de invicto en el certamen: 29 victorias y 0 derrotas y seis títulos a lo largo de su dilatada carrera. Novak vuelve a Pekín 11 años después. En su última participación derrotó a Rafael Nadal en la final. Pekín es el único torneo, en el que Djokovic ha participado un mínimo de tres veces, en el que no conoce la derrota. Otro dato asombroso en la cita es que ha decantado a su favor los últimos 27 sets disputados. Para encontrar al último jugador que le ganó un parcial hay que remontarse a Fernando Verdasco, en la segunda ronda de 2013. El tenista de Belgrado es el undécimo del ranking. Perdió su condición de 'top10' al despedirse en el estreno del US Open con el argentino Mariano Navone.

articles.summary: El malagueño, campeón en junio sobre la hierba de Mallorca, remonta un set al georgiano Basilashvili
articles.body: E l tenis masculino español, que suma cinco títulos en la presente temporada, dos de Carlos Alcaraz y uno de Alejandro Davidovich, Rafa Jódar y Dani Mérida, buscará este martes la sexta corona de 2026. Será en la final del Open 250 de Chengdu, con Davidovich de protagonista. El malagueño, de 27 años, ha regresado al circuito con fuerza tras un parón de 72 días por una lesión en la espalda. Se convierte en el tercer miembro de la 'Armada' que llega tan lejos en el certamen chino tras Albert Ramos (2016) y Pablo Carreño (2019). El veterano Basilashvili, el 121 del ranking ATP y procedente de la previa, recordó, por momentos, la mejor versión del tenista que luce cinco trofeos en su palmarés como profesional. El georgiano se anotó la manga inicial y obligó al pupilo de Pepo Clavet a firmar una remontada que cerró con un marcador de 4-6, 6-4 y 6-3, en 1 hora y 59 minutos. Es la séptima final de Davidovich y la segunda del curso tras la ganada en el Mallorca Championships. Este martes espera en la última ronda de Chengdu al ganador de la segunda semifinal que cruzará a Hubert Hurkacz y Denis Shapovalov. Los tres partidos ganados por el de Fuengirola en el inicio de la gira asiática le permiten llegar hasta los 1.845 puntos, situándose el 26 de las listas por delante de Alexander Blockx y Karen Khachanov.

articles.title: Serena and Venus Williams changed tennis together: The remarkable family story that began on Compton’s public courts and transformed the sport forever
articles.summary: Discover how Serena and Venus Williams transformed tennis from humble beginnings on Compton's public courts to global champions, reshaping women's sports forever. Their incredible journey includes 30 Grand Slam singles titles and an unmatched doubles partnership, inspiring generations of athletes.
articles.body: Serena Williams and Venus Williams didn't take the traditional tennis route to elite status. The Williams sisters began their journey on the public courts of Compton, California, where their father, Richard Williams, had a grand plan for his girls and started coaching them at an early age. And before either sister turned professional, the family’s approach was to discipline, repeat and be resilient.Their unusual start eventually made for a remarkable chapter in tennis history for their careers. Venus Williams is a seven-time Grand Slam singles champion and Serena Williams is a 23-time Grand Slam singles champion. They also made an exceptional doubles partnership, winning 14 Grand Slam doubles titles and three Olympic gold medals.Venus Williams and Serena Williams transformed tennis from Compton courts into a global sporting legacyThe story of the Williams sisters was constructed away from the sport’s traditional elite training environment. Richard Williams introduced tennis to Venus Williams and Serena Williams at a young age and built a structure around their development. They were trained early on with a major period in the public courts of Compton, and their family was very involved in their progression.The Williams family did not rely on the established junior tennis system, but forged its own path. The sisters trained together, competed against each other and developed contrasting but compatible strengths. Venus, the elder sister, was a huge influence on Serena and Serena’s competitive fire also spurred Venus on to keep improving.That relationship came to be one of the defining features of their careers. They would later meet on the other side of the net in the biggest tournaments, including Grand Slam finals, but their doubles partnership demonstrated how well they could work together on the same side of the court. They had a combined record of 14-0 in Grand Slam doubles finals, according to WTA records.Richard Williams shaped Venus Williams and Serena WilliamsRichard Williams was instrumental in shaping the course of both careers. He coached his daughters with the aim of preparing them for professional tennis, but also with an eye to building confidence and discipline. The early development of the sisters was thus closely connected to a family structure in which tennis was viewed as a long-term project rather than simply a childhood activity.Venus Williams was the first to reach the pro tour, turning pro in 1994. In 1995, Serena Williams followed suit, launching a professional career that would eventually result in 73 singles titles and 23 Grand Slam singles titlesVenus Williams and Serena Williams changed tennis foreverEach sister achieved great things independently, but their combined record made their story unique. Serena Williams finished her career with 23 Grand Slam singles titles, while Venus Williams had seven, and Venus also claimed five singles titles at Wimbledon, solidifying her legacy as one of the game’s defining players of her generation.AchievementVenus Williams and Serena WilliamsCombined Grand Slam singles titles30Grand Slam doubles titles together14Olympic doubles gold medals together3Serena Williams Grand Slam singles titles23Venus Williams Grand Slam singles titles7More broadly, their careers helped expand the cultural reach of women’s tennis. Venus Williams and Serena Williams went from public courts to championship stages at Wimbledon, the US Open and the Olympic Games, creating a family sporting story that went way beyond their individual statistics. articles.title: Tim Henman has called for changes to the calendar saying the 12-day Masters 1000 is 'too much' tennis
articles.summary: British tennis legend Tim Henman has called for changes to the calendar while Carlos Alcaraz has called directly on the ATP chairman to do something; you can watch the WTA China Open and ATP 1000 Shanghai Masters live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
World No 1 Jannik Sinner announced he will not be able to return from a knee injury as planned at the China Open next week, having not played since Wimbledon.

Carlos Alcaraz missed the French Open and Wimbledon with a wrist problem while Britain's Emma Raducanu and Jack Draper are among a number of other players who have been out for lengthy spells in 2026.

Eight of the nine Masters 1000 tournaments across the season are mandatory for most top players along with four ATP 500 events, and the growth of most Masters events to 12 days has been a bone of contention among players.

Former world No 4 Henman, who won the Masters 1000 title at the Paris Masters in 2003, would like to see changes.

"I think it's been pretty well documented that the 12-day Masters 1000s is just too much tennis," said Henman.

"That's too much time on the road and unfortunately we're seeing that with the number of players that are injured. I would definitely bring that to eight or nine days, which would free up the calendar.

"That's sort of more of a product change. I think if I had to make a practical, rule chance, then I would just get rid of the let serve.

"Every other shot can hit the top of the net, go over and in, so I would get rid of it and play it as it comes."

'ATP must do something if they want us to play important tournaments'

Alcaraz's run to the US Open quarter-finals was his first tournament since the Barcelona Open back in April after suffering a wrist injury.

Speaking in New York, the Spaniard stated: "Honestly, my break was longer than expected.

"Given the packed schedule, I obviously didn't want to stop because of an injury. However, in the future, I will take breaks, longer breaks. Maybe not four months, but one or two months, skipping certain tournaments, because it's impossible to play them all."

At the Laver Cup, which was won by Team Europe, Alcaraz said: "I think tennis has changed a lot. They have changed the balls, the courts, the speed of how we play, the movement is now more aggressive and you have to be prepared.

"We need weeks to practice and to make the physical training. There are more important tournaments making us play more and more, so I really want to takes breaks.

"Who knows what will happen in the future, but if the ATP and [chairman] Andrea Gaudenzi has to do something if they want us to play a lot of important tournaments."

Italian Flavio Cobolli is also having second thoughts about the number of tournaments he plays in.

"If you look at the number of tournaments and the number of matches we play during the year, it's not that high," he said. "We're used to playing that much. The only thing we're not used to is staying at a tournament for so many days.

"The tournament format has changed, and maybe we still need to get used to it. I've now been away from home for almost a month and a half, and even if I had gone all the way here, I would have played fewer than 10 matches."

Murray: I understand it from the players' perspective

Speaking to Sky Sports Tennis , Jamie Murray said: "I can totally understand it from the players' perspective. The Tour is longer than it's ever been in terms of commitment and days away from home.

"These younger guys have seen how Roger [Federer] and Rafael [Nadal] have elongated their careers - how they finished their careers as well. If they want to play until they're 34, 35, 36, they will probably have to skip tournaments and that's something the Tour needs to consider.

"The Tour is catering for over a hundred players and they want to be out there competing."

articles.title: Italia vence a la España de Ferrer y Robredo en la Copa de Leyendas de Albacete
articles.standfirst: El evento tuvo formato de Copa Davis
articles.summary: El evento tuvo formato de Copa Davis
articles.body: Italia, con con Andreas Seppi y Marco Cecchinato, se impuso por 2-1 al combinado español formado David Ferrer y Tommy Robredo en la IV Copa Leyendas del Tenis en Albacete, que en esta ocasión apostó por un formato de Copa Davis para conmemorar el 25 aniversario de la eliminatoria de Copa Davis España Uzbekistán, celebrada en Albacete, y que fue la primera en nuestro país, después de conquistar la primera ensaladera ante Australia en el Palau Sant Jordi. La pista central del club se llenó por completo, con un público entregado y que en ningún momento dejó de apoyar al equipo español. En el primer encuentro se enfrentaron Marco Cecchinato, el único tenista en activo de ambos equipos, y David Ferrer, que no pudo con la fortaleza física del tenista italiano. El primer set estuvo igualado hasta que Cecchinato hizo un break en el quinto juego, que le valió para hacerse con la primera manga por 6-3. En el segundo set la ruptura llegó con 2-2, Ferer la recuperó pero el transalpino volvió a adelantarse. Al final, 6-3, 6-3 en hora y 20 minutos. El segundo partido, entre Tommy Robredo y Andrea Seppi, fue más disputado y entretenido. Robredo se anotó el primer set por 6-4 y luego tuvo bola de partido con 5-3. Pero a partir de ese momento Seppi enlazó cuatro juegos consecutivos para forzar el desempate. En el supertiebreak hubo alternativas pero al final venció el italiano cerrando el partido por 4-6, 5-7 y 10/8. Una vez decidida la eliminatoria se decidió disputar un set de dobles para definir al ganador. La victoria fue para Ferrer y Robredo. La entrega de premios contó con la presencia institucional del presidente de Diputación, Santiago Cabañero; el concejal de deportes, Francisco Villaescusa; el director general del deporte de la Junta de Comunidades de Castilla La Mancha, Carlos Yuste; el subdelegado del gobierno, Miguel Juan Espinosa, así como varios concejales y diputados locales y provinciales. Por parte del Club Tenis Albacete estuvieron presentes su presidenta, Elena Marín y el director deportivo, Julián García, junto a representantes de patrocinadores.

articles.title: Novak Djokovic ready for tennis comeback at China Open
articles.summary: The 39-year-old will step back onto the court for a competitive match on Wednesday for the first time since the US Open.
articles.body:
Novak Djokovic says he is encouraged by the way his body has responded before the ⁠China Open as ⁠the 24-time tennis Grand Slam champion looks to regain momentum at a happy hunting ground after recent fitness concerns.

“Yeah, feeling good so far,” Djokovic, a six-time China Open champion, said on Monday.

Djokovic will return to action for the ⁠first time since his shock opening-round defeat by Mariano Navone at the US Open on August 30 when the 39-year-old struggled with shoulder and back problems and ⁠vomited midway through the match.

The world number 11 will look to put those problems behind him when he takes on Portugal’s Nuno Borges in the first round in Beijing this week.

“Obviously it’s completely different when you’re playing an official match compared to practice sets or practice sessions,” he said before his opening game on Wednesday.

“So far so good. I was looking forward to coming to China, as I always have. My record speaks for itself on Chinese soil. Knowing that, it also brings this dimension of confidence that I really need.

“Overall, it’s been really good so far with the body, the way ⁠I’m feeling and playing.”

The former world number one is a ⁠massive draw in Beijing, where he won the title in 2009, 2010, 2012, 2013, 2014 and 2015 and holds a 29-0 win-loss record at the ATP 500 tournament.

The pursuit of a record-extending 25th Grand ⁠Slam title remains one of the few major targets left for Djokovic, who has become increasingly selective about his tournament ⁠schedule in recent years.

“At this stage of my career, it’s really also about the tournaments where I enjoy to play, where I’ve had the success in the past, where I feel like I’m also welcomed by the fans in a positive light, in a ‌positive way,” Djokovic said.

“The history of my results on Chinese soil has been incredible. I haven’t played here in 11 years. I was trying to make it work in ‌the ‌past years with the schedule, but it worked in such a way where I played only Shanghai.

“This year, Beijing was on the priority list.”
